Expected values or observations at new sampling units

predict.magComp.Rd

Constructs posterior predictions at new units, including every fitted regression, group, spatial, and composition-factor term. See magCompPrediction for the returned quantities and the distinction between expected values and simulated observations.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'magComp'
predict(object, newdata,
                          type = NULL,
                          target = c("expected", "observation"),
                          summary = c("mean", "samples", "quantile"),
                          area = NULL, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
                          total_count = NULL, n_draws = NULL,
                          keep_effects = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted magComp object.

newdata

A data frame with one row per prediction unit, containing the covariates, group labels, and coordinates required by the fitted model.

type

Quantities to return; see magCompPrediction for supported choices. With NULL, defaults depend on the fitted components.

target

Use "expected" for conditional means based on posterior and new latent-effect draws, or "observation" to simulate observations from the fitted likelihood.

summary

Return means, aligned retained samples, or quantiles. Means and quantiles pool all retained draws across chains.

area

Prediction exposure: a positive finite scalar, a numeric vector with one value per row, or the name of a column in newdata. For fixedAreaStems, exposure is the sampling area for each predicted count. If omitted, the area column named in the fitted design must be in newdata. For pointBasalArea, supply exposure 1 / BAF, or omit area and supply the fitted design's BAF column in newdata. Training exposures are never silently reused. Exposure is required for count predictions or observation simulation when magnitude is fitted. For composition-only models, it is required only for conditional density; probabilities and conditional counts need no exposure.

probs

One or more probabilities strictly between zero and one, used for summary = "quantile".

total_count

For composition-only models, a numeric vector with one nonnegative integer total per prediction row, or the name of its column in newdata. Named vectors are matched to prediction unit IDs; unnamed vectors follow row order. Counts must not exceed R's integer limit. Required for conditional counts, conditional densities, or any observation target. Totals are treated as known and are not simulated. Not used when magnitude is fitted.

n_draws

Number of retained posterior draws to use per chain. The default NULL uses all retained draws. A positive integer selects approximately evenly spaced draws from each chain and must not exceed the number available. Selection preserves matching parameters and latent effects, and does not change the fitted object.

keep_effects

Retain the parameter and latent-effect draws used for prediction, for extraction with samples. Requires summary = "samples". Defaults to FALSE to avoid storing additional arrays. Both expected and observation targets are supported.

...

Must be empty. Unknown arguments are rejected.

Details

Prediction draws new latent effects conditional on each retained posterior draw. Thus even target = "expected" can require random simulation. With both components, target = "observation" additionally draws a negative-binomial total and multinomial allocation. Magnitude-only models draw only the total. Composition-only models instead allocate total_count using a multinomial draw. Their expected category counts are \(N_0 p_{0j}\), conditional on the supplied total \(N_0\); no magnitude is estimated. Expected probabilities require neither totals nor areas. Use set.seed() externally for reproducibility.

Use n_draws to reduce prediction time and memory while keeping all fitting draws for parameter summaries and diagnostics. For example, n_draws = 100 with three fitted chains generates 300 predictive draws. Selection occurs before prediction and retains every requested location in each draw, including joint spatial effects. Selection itself uses no random numbers. Output metadata$sample_ids identifies the positions selected within the original retained chains. Fewer draws increase Monte Carlo variability, especially in interval endpoints.

With keep_effects = TRUE, samples(predictions, type = "effects") extracts the stored new-unit effects, and type = "combined" adds their matching regression coefficients and loading-times-score contributions. These are the same draws used to construct the response predictions; extraction does not simulate again. All fitted latent terms are generated and retained, even when type requests only magnitude. standSummary() aggregates response draws and does not carry these location-level effects into its output.

Observed iid groups reuse posterior effect draws. Each unseen group receives one new Gaussian effect per term and posterior draw, shared by all rows in that group. Magnitude terms use their sampled variances; composition factor scores use unit variance. For space-time terms, a location includes the final time coordinate: an exact location-time match reuses its fitted effect, while a revisit at a new time receives a conditional draw. Prediction inherits the fitted covariance family and st_scale for neighbor searches. Known spatial locations reuse fitted effects, and repeated new coordinates share one sampled spatial effect per term and draw. Dense-GP prediction draws new effects jointly from their conditional Gaussian distribution. NNGP prediction orders new locations by their first coordinate, using subsequent coordinates to break ties, and uses neighbors among observed and earlier new locations in the same call. There is no conditionally independent spatial option. The NNGP approximation depends on the requested location set; separate calls omit cross-call links and do not reproduce a single joint call. Supply the complete desired support in one call when its joint uncertainty matters.

Both targets support fixedAreaStems and pointBasalArea. For point sampling, the expected total tally is \(M_0^{BA}/\mathrm{BAF}_0\); multiplying simulated tallies by BAF gives sampled basal-area estimates. Composition-only models condition on the supplied tally total. For an observed location, prediction reuses its stored spatial effect, but covariates and exposure still come from newdata and area. Use fitted() to obtain results for all original units with their original inputs.

standSummary aggregates stored density or magnitude samples using explicitly supplied represented land areas. It preserves the selected target. These weights serve a different purpose from the sampling exposures used to generate counts here. Neither function determines areas from polygons.

Value

A magCompPrediction named list with requested quantity components and metadata, even for one requested quantity. All quantities share posterior draw and chain identities. See that help page for dimensions and metadata fields.

See also

summary for summarizing stored draws; fitted, standSummary, magCompCV
